newsitem.title: UK: Dollar hits 34-month high against German mark.
newsitem.headline: Dollar hits 34-month high against German mark.

text.p: The dollar climbed above 1.70 German marks for the first time since April 1994 at the European close on Monday, continuing its relentless rise on the back of solid economic fundamentals, dealers said.
U.S. financial markets were closed for the Presidents Day holiday.

The dollar was bid up to a fresh 34-month high against the mark but failed to make much headway above 1.70 marks due to lack of follow-through buying as U.S. markets were closed for a holiday. But 1.70 marks is not the limit yet, analysts said.
"The outlook for the dollar is still positive, in view of continued economic problems in Germany and Japan," said Gerard Lyons, chief economist at DKB International.
In late trading, the dollar was at 1.7004 marks, up from 1.6880 at the European close on Friday. Against the Japanese yen, it was at 124.40, up from 124.23.
In New York trading on Friday, the dollar ended at 1.6880 marks and at 124.33 yen.

The dollar also was buoyant against the Swiss franc in European trading Monday, hitting a fresh three-year high at 1.4820 francs, up from 1.4640 late on Friday and vs. 1.4630 in New York trading on Friday.
Concerns that central banks might intervene to stem the dollar's rise put a lid on further increases against the yen.
Japan is generally believed to be the least happy with persistent dollar strength, meaning the market has focused on the Bank of Japan for possible central bank action.
But the Bundesbank last week joined the protest against further dollar gains, and its Vice President Johann-Wilhelm Gaddum said Monday he saw no reason for a weaker mark.
With traders convinced that fundamentals favour a strong dollar, unilateral -- or even concerted -- intervention is unlikely to cool their ardour, traders and analysts said.
